governance.attested_by: miso15 ct-intermediate 2026-06-27 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso14 bit-takeorpay-sigmoid)
governance.note: ONE structural lever on top of miso14 (--ct-intermediate-split), targeting the MISO CT_PEAKER under-run / CC_REGULAR over-run C1 miss. EIA-860 AUDIT FINDING: the 79 MISO CT_PEAKER units are ALL genuine simple-cycle GT/IC by prime mover + technology (none are mislabeled combined-cycle or cogeneration; Wabash Valley 57842's IGCC coal gasifier is retired, only its NG GT is operable; Marion 976's coal steam units are already a separate COAL klass). So the prime-mover CLASSIFICATION is correct -- what differs is DUTY: ~half the fleet (45 units, 9.5 GW, 52% of CT capacity) runs intermediate / near-baseload (measured CAMPD median CF >= 50%), not as true peakers. The single steep CT_PEAKER offer curve (committed 1.55x = a deliberate start-cost-recovery hurdle that holds true peakers idle, peak 13.15x) is wrong for an always-running unit, which amortizes its one start over thousands of hours: it priced their baseload energy ABOVE the CC fleet, so the LP never cleared it and CC_REGULAR over-ran. THE FIX: route the measured intermediate cohort (fleet.ct_intermediate_plants, derived from thermal_tranches_MISO.csv median_cf -- a forward-reproducible duty-role signal, NOT a pin to measured output, same admissibility class as ST_GAS_PEAKER_PLANTS) to a flatter CT_INTERMEDIATE offer curve (committed 1.00 / econ 1.00-1.20 / peak 3.00) so its always-on energy clears at intermediate load like the intermediate unit it is, while true peakers (median CF < 50, e.g. Summit Lake 1206, Lakefield Junction 7925) keep the steep CT_PEAKER curve. RESULT vs miso14 keeper (C1 grid-delivered TWh): CT_PEAKER 2023 -24.27 -> -19.57 (+4.7), 2024 -22.27 -> -12.83 (+9.4, materially closer); CC_REGULAR 2023 +14.44 -> +13.90, 2024 +20.58 -> +19.65 (the freed CT energy comes mostly from REDUCED over-import, not displaced CC, so the CC over-run is a separate residual -- see model_miss_notes). Gas under-run cut every cheap-gas year (2023 214.8 -> 218.3, 2024 226.2 -> 233.7 TWh toward EIA-923 249/258); 2024 energy-balance drift -4.37 -> -0.39 TWh (back inside +/-3.0 tol); 2023 import 41.0 -> 39.0 TWh (actual 37.9, closer). Determination NOT-YET (C1 still fails on the residual CC over-run + remaining CT/ST under), but strictly more structurally faithful than miso14 and better on the targeted CT dimension. Exceptions ledger intentionally EMPTY (same posture as miso14): every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS for a later lever.
governance.validation_note: Reproduce: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso MISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --miso-seam-flow-limit --coal-mustrun-online-pmin --coal-sync-srmc-tranche --coal-bit-sigmoid --ct-intermediate-split (the ONLY config diff vs the miso14 keeper is --ct-intermediate-split). meta.passes=[P1] (P2 commitment off). The 3-year per-plant LP OOMs a 15 GB box, so the bundle was solved year-by-year (~10 GB peak each) and assembled (per-year dispatch parquets kept, system/storage/btm concatenated, benchmarks rebuilt in place with --rebuild-benchmark -- no re-solve). CT_PEAKER C1 (model / actual TWh): 2023 6.86 / 26.43; 2024 13.6 / 26.4 region. No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals; the median-CF cohort assigns an offer SHAPE only. The CT_INTERMEDIATE multipliers (1.00/1.00-1.20/3.00) reflect an always-on unit offering near its own delivered marginal cost, not a fit to the price/volume residual.

Committed to the feature branch.

model_miss_notes: Exceptions ledger EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS for a later lever, not an accepted measured-input limitation. The now-isolated misses and their next levers: (1) CC_REGULAR OVER-RUN persists (2023 +13.9, 2024 +19.65 TWh): the intermediate-CT split raised CT_PEAKER by displacing over-IMPORT (2024 import 13.7 -> 9.6 TWh vs actual 23.1), not by displacing CC, so the CC over-run is a separate item -- a CC-hurdle / seam-deliverability lever that lets more of the mid-merit load import (2024) rather than self-supply with CC. (2) CT_PEAKER STILL UNDER (2023 -19.6, 2024 -12.8): the intermediate cohort now clears, but the remaining gap is the TRUE-peaker tail that needs scarcity/high-net-load hours to call it -- which ties to (3). (3) C3c NO SCARCITY TAIL (0 h > $200 vs 30/37/88): MISO has no ORDC/scarcity adder, so high-net-load hours never price the peak block; lowering the true-peaker peak (13.15x) raises CT volume but cannot create the price tail without scarcity pricing -- a separate structural mechanism, deliberately NOT done here (would be an unfaithful work-around). (4) 2025 dear-gas: total over-generation worsened (model gen 681 vs EIA-930 659; net interchange flips to fake export +16.3 vs actual -19.0 import). This is dominated by the PRE-EXISTING PRB coal over-run (coal 232 vs 201 EIA-923, unchanged by this lever) flagged in miso14's ledger; the +5.8 TWh extra intermediate-CT gas is a secondary contributor. 2025 per-class C1 is SKIPPED by the rubric (preliminary EIA-923 vintage), so it does not gate the determination -- consistent with weighting 2025 lightly. None is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12).
